title: The Unquiet Cipher Revisited
premise: Ada Iversen, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is pulled into a murder case when the victim is found wearing clothes stolen from Ada's own closet—clothes Ada hasn't seen since childhood. The victim turns out to be connected to a fire thirty years ago that killed Ada's parents and left Ada the sole survivor of a group home called the Cipher House. As Ada investigates, they discover the fire was arson tied to an inheritance scheme, and that one of their fellow survivors has spent decades eliminating witnesses. In the end, Ada must choose between exposing the killer—a person who once saved their life—and letting the past stay buried; they close the case, but at the cost of the found family they'd rebuilt.
about_author: Silas Iversen is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating suspicious fires in the upper Midwest before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about memory, complicity, and the documents people leave behind.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A body surfaces in the river wearing Ada's childhood coat, monogrammed with a name Ada hasn't spoken in decades. The emotional beat is cold shock—the past arriving uninvited—and Ada's professional detachment begins to crack as they realize the clothes are unmistakably theirs.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Interrogated by Detective Ruiz, Ada recalls every detail of finding the body but notices gaps: someone has been inside their apartment. The beat is unease sharpening into paranoia as Ada's perfect memory becomes both their greatest asset and a target.

chapters.title: Cipher House
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with flashback fragments. Ada returns to the ruins of the group home where six children survived a 1994 fire that killed two caretakers. The beat is grief resurfacing; Ada catalogs the survivors—Mara, Jonah, Tess, Eli, and Ruth—and realizes the victim was the home's former accountant.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Pact
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada tracks down Mara, now a hospice nurse, who insists the survivors swore never to speak of the fire. Mara warns Ada to stop digging. The beat is warmth curdling into threat—the first hint that the found family may be guarding something lethal.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Cold
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Insurance archives reveal the Cipher House was overinsured weeks before the fire, and the payout vanished through the accountant's firm. The beat is the thrill of the hunt; Ada's memory reconstructs a ledger page everyone else forgot existed.

chapters.title: Jonah's Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Now a small-town pastor, Jonah receives Ada's call and burns a letter he's kept for thirty years. The beat is dread and guilt; readers learn Jonah knows who set the fire but believes silence was mercy, not complicity.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Tess, another survivor, is found dead in a staged accident—wearing jewelry stolen from Ada's apartment. The beat is terror made personal; the killer isn't framing Ada randomly, they're dressing the dead in Ada's memories.

chapters.title: Ruiz's File
chapters.summary: Detective Ruiz's POV. Ruiz shares a sealed file: the original arson investigator ruled the fire accidental under pressure, then died mysteriously. The beat is reluctant alliance; Ruiz suspects Ada, but Ada's recall of the old case notes proves too precise to dismiss.

chapters.title: Eli's Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Eli, dying of cancer, plays a tape recorded years ago admitting he helped move money for the accountant—but swears the fire was meant to be empty. The beat is moral vertigo; survival itself starts to look like a debt Ada never knew they owed.

chapters.title: What the Child Saw
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, deep flashback. Ada's photographic memory finally unlocks the night of the fire: a fourth adult in the house, face reflected in a hallway mirror. The beat is revelation and horror—the arsonist wasn't a stranger but someone from inside the household.

chapters.title: Ruth's Garden
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth, the eldest survivor, tends her garden and her secrets, remembering how she carried little Ada out of the flames. The beat is tenderness laced with menace; Ruth's love for Ada is real, and so is her willingness to kill for it.

chapters.title: The Missing Payout
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the money offshore, Ada discovers the inheritance was meant for the children themselves—stolen by the caretakers, then reclaimed by someone else after the fire. The beat is betrayal compounded; every adult Ada trusted was already guilty.

chapters.title: Mara Breaks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered by Ada, Mara confesses she saw Ruth return to the house the night of the fire and has paid for silence ever since. The beat is collapse and relief; Mara begs Ada to run before Ruth decides Ada knows too much.

chapters.title: House Fire, Repeat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada's apartment building catches fire—an unmistakable message. Ada escapes with only their memory intact, losing every physical trace of their old life. The beat is loss and clarity; stripped of evidence, Ada realizes only testimony remains.

chapters.title: The Accountant's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The murdered accountant's daughter reveals her father kept insurance against his own killers: a sealed deposition naming Ruth as the one who collected the payout under a false identity. The beat is grim vindication shadowed by sorrow.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada maps Ruth's alibis across three decades and finds each death coincided with Ruth's charity work—her cover and her hunting ground. The beat is cold methodical fury; Ada stops investigating and starts building a trap.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth invites Ada to the rebuilt Cipher House property, ostensibly for closure, knowing what she intends. The beat is terrible intimacy; Ruth genuinely believes she is protecting Ada, the last piece of family she has left.

chapters.title: Cipher House Revisited
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the house, Ruth lays out the truth: she burned it to recover the children's stolen inheritance and has killed ever since to keep the secret—and to keep Ada safe. The beat is confrontation as confession; love and murder indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. Ruth offers Ada a choice: join the silence or die with the truth. Ada, recording everything, triggers Ruiz's arrival; Ruth, rather than be taken, walks into the old cellar where the fire began. The beat is devastating climax—justice won at the cost of the only family Ada had.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada gives formal statements, closing the insurance case and the murders, but refuses to soften the record even when it implicates the dead. The beat is weary integrity; Ada learns some cases can be closed but never finished.

chapters.title: What We Buried Together
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At a joint funeral for Ruth and the victims, the surviving survivors stand apart from Ada, unable to forgive the exposure. The beat is mourning the living; found family fractures under the weight of truth.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Cipher
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, coda. Months later, Ada takes a new case and hesitates at the door, finally understanding why they always chose unsolvable ones—to stay invisible. They knock anyway. The beat is quiet resolve; survival now means being seen, whatever it costs.
